$description: The language gate's biggest input, pinned. `/usr/share/dict` is an ambient fact of whichever machine runs the gate: the first CI run this repository ever had died there with ENOENT, and the day this file was written the one package name `wpolish` resolved to two different word lists — the Ubuntu rebuild and the 20240901-1 it rebuilds, one word apart (`email`) — while the pool had already rotated the older file out of reach. A verdict that depends on the machine is the drift `req-axis` exists against, so the dictionary becomes what `package-lock.json` is to `node_modules` and `skills-lock.json` to the vendored skills (decision 0040): this file is the material record, and the word lists it locks are restored, never tracked. `tools/restore-dictionaries.mjs` fetches each archive, verifies it, unpacks the one member named here and verifies THAT, into `tools/.dictionaries/`. The `url` is a courtesy and the sha256 is the identity: when the pool drops these files — it rotates superseded versions routinely — any mirror serving the same bytes restores the same input.
